Irene / Ben — quick notes from the payments/ops perspective: 

- For Redwood-managed hosted API endpoints we bill by consumption region; the marketplace listing fee is allocated where the meter reports usage. However, for private offers (customer-contracted list price) we can anchor billing to contract region if the private offer specifically scopes listing by contract. That is a configuration flag on the offer metadata.

- Overlap/cross-region consumption: we currently avoid double-listing the listing fee by tagging each invoice line with a marketplace-settlement tag and deduplicating when cross-region taxation applies. If Acme wants the invoice to show "contract-region list price + consumption-region usage" we can produce a two-line breakdown (contract list price line + usage line per region) but payment collection and settlement will still follow the contract anchor unless they request otherwise.

I can draft a sample invoice fragment. Ben — can you confirm tax/recognition implications of building uplift into list price vs separate credit line?

Irene / Jordan — ran a quick model and attached an XLSX with three scenarios: 1) uplift as separate reseller credit line, 2) uplift embedded in list price tiers, 3) hybrid (list price anchor + separate reseller allocation). High level: 

- Separate reseller credit line: clean accounting lane for Acme and reseller. Redwood invoices full list price to Acme, then applies a line-item credit to the reseller (negative line) which we net before remittance to marketplace. This leaves our gross revenue intact but increases gross-to-net activity (requires tracking on settlement).

- Embedded uplift: raise the list price in reseller-eligible tiers by the uplift %. Simpler for invoicing but changes our reported ASP and could affect marketplace fee % calculations. Revenue recognition stays straightforward, but partner reporting will show higher list prices.

- Hybrid: contract region anchors list price; when consumption occurs in other regions we emit separate usage lines per region and then a consolidated reseller allocation line at the invoice footnote. This is the most transparent to Acme but increases invoice complexity.

I attached 20280516-acme-listing-fee-model.xlsx with sample numbers and a suggested wording for invoice lines. For Acme's 12% uplift request, option 1 keeps their reseller bookkeeping easiest — they see an explicit 12% uplift credit. Option 2 pushes the complexity to Redwood and the marketplace (might require manual recon if they later change reseller relationships).

-ben
Senior Pricing Analyst, Redwood Inference
